concepts.why: The patient has erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and a mycological culture yielded growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes, which is a common cause of dermatophytosis.
The patient has a history of frequent contact with stray cats and has elevated IgE levels, which could indicate an allergic reaction, and the skin lesions are consistent with contact dermatitis.
The patient has elevated eosinophil counts and IgE levels, and the skin lesions are consistent with eosinophilic folliculitis, which is an inflammatory condition.
The patient has a history of frequent contact with stray cats and has skin lesions consistent with irritant contact dermatitis, which is a non-allergic inflammatory condition.
The patient has elevated IgE levels and skin lesions consistent with atopic dermatitis, which is an allergic inflammatory condition.
The patient has erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and elevated inflammatory markers, which could indicate a bacterial infection such as cellulitis.
The patient has erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions and elevated inflammatory markers, which could indicate a bacterial infection such as impetigo.
The patient has skin lesions consistent with seborrheic dermatitis, which is an inflammatory condition.

rationales.F04: The presence of erythematous, infiltrating, well-demarcated skin lesions is a common feature of several dermatological conditions.
rationales.F05: Frequent contact with stray cats may increase the risk of dermatophytosis.
rationales.F09: Elevated eosinophil count is often associated with eosinophilic folliculitis and atopic dermatitis.
rationales.F10: High IgE levels are commonly seen in atopic dermatitis.
rationales.F11: The growth of Trichophyton mentagrophytes in mycological culture is diagnostic of dermatophytosis.
